title: Corpus selection record and admission receipt
description: The input contract for a corpus, in two content-addressed records, adopting the split proposed in inbox/Q-0001 section 3 and ruled accepted in outbox/A-0004 (ruling 5). The root of this schema is the selection record (SHARED_50_DEAL_SELECTION/V1): the immutable, Ben-approved statement of which deals a corpus contains. The producer's admission results go in a separate record, $defs/admissionReceipt (CORPUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT/V1), so that admitting a deal never rewrites the approved selection or changes its identity. Neither of these is the corpus manifest inside a released package; that is deal-terms-package.schema.json#/$defs/corpusManifest. Every ID is contentId(domain, record) or sha256Hex(bytes) as defined in the producer's lib/canonical-v2/canonical-bytes.js.

corpus_id.description: contentId('SHARED_50_DEAL_SELECTION/V1', this record without corpus_id). Approval fields are inside the payload, so an unapproved draft and the approved selection are different records with different IDs. That is deliberate: only an approved selection has a corpus_id worth citing.

required_deal_count.description: Must equal deals.length. A selection that does not contain the number of deals it declares is not a selection.

selection_rule_version.description: The governed rule ID under which these deals were chosen.

ben_approval_id.description: Content ID of Ben's approval record. The one addition to Q-0001's shape: approved_by and approved_on say who and when, this says which ruling, so approval is verifiable rather than a name in a string. Corpus composition is Ben's call and no agent may synthesise this value.

deals.description: Ordered by ordinal, which runs 0..n-1 without gaps. deal_id is unique across the selection.

hex64.description: A 64-character lowercase hexadecimal digest: sha256Hex(bytes) or contentId(domain, record).

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key, zero-padded to ten digits.

admissionState.description: PROPOSED: in the approved selection, not yet admitted. ADMITTED: an admission receipt entry binds the canonical text. REJECTED: admission was attempted and failed. WITHDRAWN: removed before admission.

transactionAnchor.description: The first executed transaction document. An explicit, immutable selection: a later-discovered source cannot change it.

agreement_role.description: The consumer's role label for this document within the deal, for example merger_agreement.

document_name.description: The SEC document name. Permitted here because this record is an input, not a package. A released package never carries it: packages identify documents by role and content, and their verifier rejects anything file-name shaped.

deal_id.description: The consumer-minted transaction-level deal ID: sha256Hex(canonicalJson(PUBLIC_MA_DEAL/V1 payload)) over target_cik, transaction_anchor and announced_transaction_ordinal. The producer never mints or reissues it. This is the value a released package carries as transaction_id.

source_admission_manifest_id.description: Content ID of the SOURCE_ADMISSION_MANIFEST/V2 record produced by lib/canonical-v2/sec-source-admission.js.

admission_receipt_id.description: Content ID of the SOURCE_ADMISSION_PREPARATION_RECEIPT/V1 record, whose terminal_status must be PASS.

receipt_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the receipt's committed bytes. The content ID proves what the record says; this proves which bytes said it.

deal_id.description: The selected deal this admission belongs to. Must appear in the selection record named by corpus_id.

deal_key.description: The producer's per-document key: contentId('DEAL_TERMS_DEAL_KEY/V1', {source_system, issuer_cik, accession, document_role_key}) for the required agreement being admitted. This is where the consumer's transaction-level identity and the producer's document-level identity meet.

admissionReceipt.$comment: CORPUS_ADMISSION_RECEIPT/V1. Adds admission results without rewriting the selection record.

corpus_id.description: The selection record this receipt admits against. A receipt is bound to one selection and never carries over to another.

selection_record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the selection record's committed bytes, alongside its content ID, for the same reason receipt_sha256 exists.

producer_run_id.description: The producer run that performed the admissions. Which extraction route was used is recorded here, not in the selection.

admissions.description: Ordered by deal_key. One entry per required agreement of each selected deal.
